_comment: Scripts no build surface invokes, accounted for by hand (issue #1028).
`scripts/verify-coverage-check.py` derives everything it can: a script a
Makefile target invokes is `gate` or `excluded` by whether `make verify`
reaches that target, and one a .woodpecker.yml step invokes is `ci`. This
file is the remainder - the scripts the tree cannot answer for - and a new
file in `scripts/` reds that gate until it has a target or an entry here.
THREE CLASSES, AND ONE OF THEM IS CROSS-CHECKED:
tested         a module under tests/ drives it, so `make test` - which IS
in `make verify` - exercises it. `consumer` names that module.
runtime        a command or hook reads its verdict at run time; no build
gate exercises it. `consumer` names that surface. The closing
report counts these, because they are the honest gap.
not-a-checker  it issues no verdict at all. Reported nowhere - which is why
it is the one class checked against ADR 0008's census: a
script the census enumerates as an instrument cannot be
filed here, so parking a checker where the report never
names it costs a red instead of a silence.
`consumer` IS A CLAIM, NOT A SENTENCE. The gate opens the named path and
searches it for the script's own name, so an entry goes STALE when the
consumer is deleted or stops mentioning it - which is exactly how a
hand-written justification usually rots.
A `tested` entry asserts that the named module drives the SCRIPT, not that
it mentions the name. Several modules name a script only as a fixture or an
allowlist member; those are not what makes a green load-bearing, and they do
not belong here.

flow-driver-retirement-check.sh.reason: refuses to retire a driver whose obligations are unaccounted

flow-live-driver-guard.sh.reason: reports whether another session is mid-implementation in this checkout

flow-pr-watch.sh.reason: classifies a PR's checks for the wave merge queue, in another session

flow-stale-check.sh.reason: reports whether the base moved under an in-flight branch

flow-start-resolve.sh.reason: decides whether a checkout is created, entered or taken over

flow-wave-lexicon.sh.reason: accepts or rejects a wave transition token

flow-wave-plan.py.reason: the startable set and path-contention index an orchestrator hands out

flow-wave-registry.sh.reason: role-to-address resolution read by a different session

flow-wave-residuals.py.reason: decides whether a residual candidate becomes an issue after the wave

flow-worktree-guard.sh.reason: blocks a commit when an edit leaked into the main tree

flow-worktree-sweep.sh.reason: decides whether another session's checkout is removed

friction-log.sh.reason: appends a friction record, fail-open by design; it issues no verdict

gate-lib.sh.reason: the shared argument and verdict module (#1126); its --check self-check is driven by controls/gate-lib through make negative-controls, and its refusals are driven directly by the test module named here

gh-pr-merge.sh.reason: decides whether the squash lands on main

hook-mask-output.sh.reason: the PostToolUse masking hook; it rewrites output and issues no verdict

hook-pending-retro.sh.reason: an opt-in advisory reminder; it issues no verdict

hook-permission-census.sh.reason: the PermissionRequest census hook and its vendored copy of the risk taxonomy

knowledge-graduation-check.py.reason: decides whether a completed spec may be removed

lane-serveability-check.sh.reason: decides whether /qwen:auto and /gemma:auto delegate at all

mcp-drift.py.reason: compares configured MCP servers with the checkout

measurement-shape-scan.py.reason: warn counts the retro folds into classification without re-scanning

npm-global-upgrade.sh.reason: reports the harness version transition rather than npm's exit code

playwright-desk.py.reason: leases a browser desk, or refuses; /browser:session acts on the result

sandbox-phase1-trial.sh.reason: a one-off sandbox trial harness; it issues no verdict
